clusters.theme: U1 reference-contract conflict: the friction ledger is "never read" yet a nudge must read it
clusters.note: Same conflict reported at three separate session starts, by the same step, never resolved between them.

cases.what: Contract conflict: evolve-system.md says the friction log is append-only and must never be read, but new-session's evolve-nudge precondition ('friction-log.ndjson carries records for it') can only be evaluated by reading it — so deriving the nudge required reading a file the same system forbids reading.

evolve-system.md mandates the friction log is append-only and 'never load prior records', while new-session's evolve-nudge condition requires knowing whether friction-log.ndjson carries records for a candidate epoch - evaluating the nudge meant reading it (144 records across 2 epochs). Latent contradiction: here the frozen-entries condition failed for both candidate epochs anyway, so the read was avoidable by short-circuit ordering, but on a fully-frozen complete epoch the read is unavoidable

Two references disagree on reading the friction file: evolve-system.md says append-only, never read it or load prior records, while new-session's evolve-nudge condition requires checking whether friction-log.ndjson carries records for a completed epoch. Resolved by an aggregate epoch/count tally (no record content loaded).

clusters.theme: U2 a reference misdescribes its own mechanism (phantom variable · loose guard · off-by-a-phase window · wrong field path)
clusters.note: Five distinct sites: fan-out.md {output_path} (x2), the pending-exists grep guard, the report Commits window, the matrix status field path.

cases.what: fan-out.md lists {output_path} among the variables to substitute but the distiller prompt body never references it, while the body does contain {plan} and {section} inside the quoted citation-format example - which are illustrative, not variables. The mandated self-check for unsubstituted braces therefore needs a judgment call in both directions on every run: one listed variable with no slot, two slots that must be left alone. Cost nothing here (agents cited correctly) but the check cannot be applied literally as written.

The report's Commits field is sourced from 'commit subjects since state.yaml.last_wrap', but wrap writes last_wrap in P6 and commits in P7 — so the previous chunk's commit always falls inside the window and a literal reading would attribute it to the chunk being wrapped. Caught by checking the commit subject against the chunk marker; the report states the chunk has no commits yet and names 2cdec9e as the prior chunk's.

The pending-exists Setup guard is prone to a false positive: master-route.md carries a template legend line ({status: pending|complete}) containing the literal word 'pending', so a plain grep for it returns a hit on a master with zero pending records; a second precise grep was needed to clear the guard

fan-out.md's substitution list names {output_path} among the variables to substitute, but the distiller prompt template contains no {output_path} placeholder — the self-check for unsubstituted braces passed regardless and the orchestrator writes the extract files itself; absorbed at zero cost, flagged as a reference-file inconsistency

Coverage probe read status as a top-level capability field per the skill body's 'chunk:null & status:planned' shorthand; the matrix nests it at verification.status, so the first parse returned 32 rows with status None and had to be reformulated.

clusters.theme: U3 a count or claim derived from a non-authoritative view reaches a decision or the user
clusters.note: Truncated console views, hand-rolled regex/dict derivations, and citations to documents that do not hold the fact. Two were caught only by the operator; one required a public retraction.

cases.what: The code-graph calls view SILENTLY UNDER-REPORTS cross-crate call sites. Querying callers of Scenario::from_toml_str returned 1 production caller (conductor-cli/paths.rs:78) plus in-file test callers; a grep cross-check found 5 production call sites across 4 crates, missing conductor-core/scenario_catalog.rs:47, conductor-run/src/lib.rs:420, conductor-tauri/src/commands.rs:79 and :344, and conductor-timeline/tests/replay.rs:26. Had the graph been trusted, the plan would have concluded a signature change was cheap and set a wrong constraint on a keystone chunk. A zero-rows result is documented as a real finding; a LOW-but-nonzero rows result has no such guidance and reads as authoritative.

RETRACTION - the earlier claim that the code-graph calls view under-reports cross-crate call sites is FALSE and must not reach curation. The trace shows q4 calls and q5 refs each returned 41 rows for from_toml_str, db_state=fresh, across 6 files in 5 crates; the rows=1 belonged to q3 (pid_format). The 1 was produced by piping q4 output through head -30, which cut 41 records to 10, leaving conductor-cli/paths.rs as the only visible non-test caller - then attributing that to the graph. The same habit corrupted the PId finding: q1 carried a self-imposed LIMIT 40 and returned exactly 40, which was read as the complete set and written up as no references outside the test module; the true count is 82 refs across 16 files in 6 crates. grep did not beat the graph - grep over-counts (pub fn definition, 4 test-function names, 1 doc comment). The real friction is an orchestrator reading a self-truncated view as a result set and blaming the tool. Operator caught it before apply. Artifacts corrected: research.md Graph impact (with an inline correction note), plan.md Implementation notes and Provenance; the generalized grep-before-trusting-the-graph directive was removed and replaced with the narrow true lesson (SCIP matches by descriptor; attribute a row count to its query; never read a LIMIT-ed or head-ed view as the result; graph lines are 0-indexed vs grep 1-indexed).

plan.md reached review with two citations pointing at documents that do not hold the cited fact, both caught by the operator, neither catchable by any mechanical check. (a) The wrap-amendment note said security-plan carries derived anyhow gate wording and must be amended in lockstep - carried verbatim from the arch extract, which reads only architecture.md and was therefore speculating about a document outside its remit; verification found 10 anyhow hits in security-plan and zero carrying a version. (b) An acceptance criterion cited security-plan section Accepted exceptions for the count 17, merging an artifact-derived number (deny.toml) with a spec-derived rule under one citation; that section names exactly 1 ignore + 1 allow. Consequence under drift=0 would have been an amendment aimed at a non-existent target, or spec churn authoring version wording into an already-correct document

The lock-delta verification script keyed a dict by package NAME, but Cargo.lock legitimately holds the same name at multiple versions, so duplicate names collapsed and the comparison reported a self-contradictory result: 559 packages before vs 514 after alongside 'ADDED: none, REMOVED: none'. Caught by the impossible arithmetic and redone as a multiset diff over name+version pairs plus git diff as the authority, which showed the true delta (559 pairs unchanged in count, exactly 4 swapped). A name-keyed comparison silently under-reports lock changes and must not be used to verify a lock-only chunk

A graph-impact citation reached the user review factually wrong: the crate_edges row COUNT was taken correctly from the trace (6) but the direction SPLIT was reconstructed from a tail-truncated console view, inferring an outbound edge that does not exist (all 6 rows are inbound; conductor-run was outside the visible window). Honouring the trace for counts but not for content is the same failure as reading a truncated view as the result. No active validation check catches this — validation.md §7 explicitly defers the citation-resolve gate to a future escalation rung — so the operator's review was the only thing between the error and implement's input. Corrected at 4 sites across plan.md and research.md.

The tests extract's literal-60 inventory was correct but not complete: a first-hand grep found 8 further doc/help sites it did not list, one of which (cli.rs:49) is user-visible clap help text rather than a comment, plus a false positive to guard (render.rs:42 Lamp::Blocked => 60 is an ANSI color code)

a hand-written regex over coverage.rs undercounted Auto rows as 42; the true count is 43 (82 rows total). Caught only by cross-checking against the roll-up the prior chunk shipped, then re-derived with a stricter parse - a derived count that no independent number contradicted would have entered research.md and the plan silently

clusters.theme: U4 an invocation's own mechanics silently aborted or misdirected the work
clusters.note: &&-chain wholesale abort on an expected-absent optional path; heredoc backslash mangling on Git-Bash/Windows; a cargo tree -e filter hiding the real edge behind a misleading hint.

cases.what: A single && -chained health-probe batch aborted wholesale (exit 2) on an expected-absent OPTIONAL path (the CLAUDE.md two-location pre-flight probes .claude/CLAUDE.md, which does not exist here), discarding the remaining checks in the batch; re-run with ; separators

cargo tree -i crossbeam-epoch -e normal,build printed 'nothing to print' plus a hint to try --target all, misdirecting diagnosis toward a target-platform cause; the actual cause was the -e normal,build filter excluding the dev edge (assert_fs). Re-ran without -e to find the path

Backslash sequences do not survive a quoted bash heredoc into Python in this Git-Bash-on-Windows path: a host-path regex failed twice with an incomplete-escape error on \U, a raw string did not fix it, and the reported error position did not correspond to any backslash in the intended pattern. The same hazard then corrupted two friction-log appends built as shell-quoted JSON (bare \U reaching the file as an invalid JSON escape) and again broke the first repair attempt. Only building every backslash with chr(92) worked

clusters.theme: U5 an acceptance criterion or decision input is misrouted in time or remit
clusters.note: The matrix decides a P4 choice but is read at P5; an obs acceptance names an artifact the chosen mechanism never produces; a criterion cites evidence no listed Test Command emits.

cases.what: A verification-matrix capability (v2-28, stale rmcp wording) bore directly on a P4 scope decision, but the matrix is in no distiller's input set and not in research's remit, and the skill schedules its read at P5 step 4 AFTER the decision it informs; a keyword-filtered grep over the matrix missed v2-28 and only an unfiltered listing of all 32 titles surfaced it. Knowing v2-28 is scoped to three DOCUMENTS reversed the premise of the rmcp option from 'a later chunk owns this' to 'no acceptance would catch a manifest line'

An acceptance criterion referenced evidence no Test Command produces: the obs criterion asserts logs/agent-latest.jsonl carries the 7 base fields, is host-path-free and panic-free, but the plan's listed gates are agent-run.sh run (which emits that artifact only when SCENARIO is set) and agent-run.sh status. Verifying it required choosing an unlisted producer - an explicit --agent-mode run - at the smoke step

obs acceptance contribution 1 requires the posture be machine-parseable from an obs artifact via jq/serde_json, but the chosen mechanism is a Rust const plus a nextest gate (not an obs artifact) and the coverage roll-up is Markdown text (not JSON) - no option literally satisfies it. Resolved by carrying the derived count onto all three roll-up surfaces, satisfying the intent rather than the letter; P2's aggregate checks cannot catch an AC that no design can literally meet
